title: the EASTL basic_string<char> static initialisers, one row per member
heading: ## Per-member rows: the static string object each EASTL basic_string<char> initialiser builds (OPUS, 2026-10-03)
lead: The family `EASTL basic_string<char> static initialisers` (frontmatter: 51 members; {N} get a row here) shares one form, not repeated per row: it builds a named allocator with `001EDF00` (twice: a stack temporary, then the allocator at `S+0x18`), zeroes the static string object S (qwords `+0`, `+8` and `+0x10`), and copies a literal into it: for a length above 1 it allocates through the allocator's slot `+0x10` and stores begin, end and capacity at `S+0`, `S+8` and `S+0x10`, otherwise it points S at the empty-string sentinel `02EBA2E0`; it then tail-jumps to `00808B90` with its teardown (the atexit registration). All 51 make exactly these external calls. What differs from member to member is S: no two members initialise the same object. Each row anchors the member's `movdqu` that zeroes S (its distinguishing instruction) and states S and the literal it copies (loaded with `lea rsi`; several members copy the same text into different objects). All are read from the certified image. {CHECK} re-derives every row and compares it with the committed {ROWS}. Two controls are refused: a swapped value and a moved anchor. Members that do not derive are listed in [`excluded.tsv`](../../_index/candidates/opus-ee-eastl-string-initialisers-1003/excluded.tsv).
